question_prefix: When should a Universal Forwarder be used instead of a Hea
explanation: A Universal Forwarder (UF) is the lightweight choice; it collects and forwards raw data with minimal processing. A Heavy Forwarder (HF) runs the full parsing pipeline and is required when you must transform data at the edge. NOTE: the marked answer appears incorrect - filtering/routing and masking (anonymizing/SEDCMD) are parsing-pipeline operations that require a Heavy Forwarder, so 'When most of the data needs filtering' (C) actually describes an HF use case, not a UF one. A UF is the right choice for high-velocity sources or simple forwarding where no parsing-time transformation is needed; database (DB Connect) and LDAP inputs are modular inputs that also require an HF.

question_prefix: Which index-time props.conf attributes impact indexing per
explanation: LINE_BREAKER and SHOULD_LINEMERGE are index-time (parsing) settings that govern how the incoming stream is split into events, so they directly affect indexing performance - SHOULD_LINEMERGE in particular forces the more expensive line-merging logic on the indexer/heavy forwarder. REPORT is a search-time field-extraction directive and has no effect on indexing throughput. ANNOTATE_PUNCT only toggles whether the punct field is created and has negligible impact compared to event/line breaking.

question_prefix: How can a Splunk admin control the logging level for a spec
explanation: The noop command's log_<level> argument lets you set the debug logging channel for a single search run without needing CLI access or changing server-wide settings, e.g. | noop log_debug=* raises the log level for that search's processors. Splunk applies the log level after parsing the noop command, so it can take effect even when noop is placed after the base search. The server settings page (A) and log-local.cfg change logging globally, not per-search; infocsv_log_level (B) only affects the intermediate results CSV, and the Job Inspector (D) inspects a completed job rather than changing its log level.

question_prefix: Based on the data sizing and retention parameters listed be
explanation: Index storage is estimated as (daily ingest x compression factor x retention days) plus padding. Here that is 20 GB/day x 0.5 x 30 days = 300 GB, plus 100 GB padding = 400 GB, which is option C. Option A multiplies the padding by the compression factor (wrong - padding is added after). Option B omits the compression factor entirely, and option D divides by the factor instead of multiplying, inflating the result.

explanation: The data 'to be indexed' is the event data in transit from forwarders to the indexers, so enabling TLS on the forwarder-to-indexer connection is what encrypts that ingested data on the wire. Browser-to-Splunk-Web (A) secures the UI session, not the data being indexed. Deployment server to clients (C) secures app/config distribution, and indexer cluster peer-node traffic (D) covers replication between indexers rather than the inbound data feed itself.

question_prefix: Where in the Job Inspector can details be found to help det
explanation: In the Search Job Inspector, the 'Execution costs' section lists each processing component (for example command.search.index, command.search.rawdata, dispatch.evaluate) with the time and invocation counts each consumed, making it the place to pinpoint where a search spends its time. The Search Job Properties fields like runDuration and runtime give a total elapsed figure but do not break down where time was spent, and Total Events Matched is a volume metric rather than a performance breakdown.

question_prefix: When implementing KV Store Collections in a search head clu
explanation: In a search head cluster the KV Store runs its own cluster with a KV Store captain (primary), which is a role distinct from the search head cluster captain. When collection content changes, the KV Store primary coordinates with the SHC captain so that updates are replicated consistently across members. The KV Store primary and SHC captain are not guaranteed to be the same node (ruling out A/C), and members do not update their copies independently (ruling out D); the 50-member limit applies to the KV Store cluster size, not to whether changes are allowed.

question_prefix: Which component in the splunkd.log will log information rel
explanation: The AggregatorMiningProcessor is the parsing-pipeline component that performs event aggregation/breaking, so it is what logs WARN messages about bad event breaking, such as 'Breaking event because limit of 256 (MAX_EVENTS) has been exceeded'. EventBreaking is not the splunkd.log component name for these warnings, IndexingPipeline is a broader pipeline label rather than the event-breaking processor, and AuditTrail relates to audit logging of user/system activity.
